payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make this look like a comic book photo
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Compared with the source, does the edited image visibly use comic-book visual styling?
node.criteria: Pass if the edited image has recognizable comic-book visual treatment absent from the source, such as visibly stylized contours or graphic color treatment; fail if that treatment is absent or only a grain/filter effect; unknown if the comparison is not observable.
node.source_quote: Make this look like a comic book photo
node.endpoint: The image visibly has comic-book visual styling.
node.necessity: The instruction explicitly requests a comic-book look; without visible comic-book styling, that requested transformation is incomplete.

node_traces.evidence: Compared with the source, the edited street scene retains ordinary photographic detail and muted colors. It shows no recognizable comic-book contours, halftone shading, or graphic color treatment; the visible change is mainly darker/grainier texture.

d2: The node checks only whether photographic appearance is retained, so it can pass even when the requested comic-book treatment is absent. The trace supports that narrow finding, but the edited image appears largely like the source photograph with modest contrast/color changes; it does not establish a comic-book visual treatment. Make the decision criterion assess both parts of the combined request—visible comic-book styling and retained photographic subject matter—and distinguish complete fulfillment from partial progress rather than treating photographic retention alone as success. Keep the reference label as an aggregate constraint, not atomic ground truth: the current trace is valid and high-confidence, with no transport or dependency failure, so investigate the criterion’s incomplete coverage and how it contributes to the aggregate disagreement rather than overriding the visual evidence.

response.content: {"text":"The criterion already directly tests the requested comic-book styling, and the trace is valid, high-confidence, and supported by the source/edited comparison: the edit mainly darkens or adds grain, without recognizable graphic treatment. Do not broaden it to require “retained photographic subject matter”; that is not an explicit separate requirement in “comic book photo.” Instead, inspect the executable node’s actual criterion and binding, since the supplied node says to fail when comic styling is absent but the downstream diagnostic claims it checks only photographic retention. Resolve that mismatch so the executed check evaluates visible comic-book styling against the source, with unknown reserved for unobservable comparisons. Treat the aggregate “partial” label as a signal to investigate how modest changes are counted as progress, not as proof that comic styling is present or a reason to override the visual evidence. There is no transport, schema, or dependency failure indicated."}
